title: Loopforge / Field Instrument
status: Alternative art-direction board for review; not selected production art.
exact_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one detailed art-director style sheet for the Loopforge factory camera-console, an alternative direction for review. Create one landscape 3:2 board at high detail.

Input images:
1. LIMEN original character sheet: identity reference only. Mechanical cracked blue-black skull, visible mechanical jaw teeth, cyan optics, industrial shoulder armour.
2. STILETTO original character sheet: identity reference only. Closed angular dark helmet, narrow glowing red-orange horizontal visor with short central vertical stem, NO exposed human face, sleek mechanical neck.
3. Loopforge forge room: material/world reference only; use its oil, hot metal, soot, dense machinery and amber work lighting. Do NOT place room art in the monitor.
4. Baseline camera-console style sheet: useful board content and readability reference, NOT its geometry. Develop a materially different industrial object.

Primary request: FIELD INSTRUMENT / retro-industrial field equipment. Broad inspiration from tactile mid-century portable diagnostic instruments and Pip-Boy-like physical controls, but create original Loopforge industrial construction: NO Fallout/Vault-Tec logos, no Vault Boy, no franchise symbols, no copied game interface. Battered olive enamel, warm brown bakelite grips and selector knobs, thick serviceable casting, captive screws, protected thumb switches, honest seams, cable ferrules, recessed analog hardware. More rounded cast-machine housing and instrument engineering than the baseline's rectangular brass plate assembly. Serious cinematic material realism, mature detailed dystopia, not cartoon, not a generic website UI, not steampunk ornament.

Composition: unified charcoal drafting-board backdrop, restrained warm-ivory condensed technical headings, generous clear space. Header exactly "LOOPFORGE / FIELD INSTRUMENT". One large nearly front-on OFF camera monitor dominates the upper-left half, filling roughly half the board width. Its broad olive cast housing has curved structural corners, a few exposed slotted captive fasteners, warm brown bakelite side grip and tactile lower selector knob with unlit mechanical detents. The monitor glass is BLACK EMPTY UNPOWERED GLASS, with only faint soft studio glare from top-left and subtle dust confined to edges. Absolutely no room, no scene, no silhouettes, no waveform, no static, no digits, no statuses, no REC, no LOCKED or OFF badge inside or on this off camera. Directly under the glass, adhered to lower physical bezel, is a worn torn cream tape label hand-written in dark pen exactly "LATTICE FORGE". Legible letters with small human baseline drift and worn pen pressure; no printed stencil for room names.

On upper right, show compact authored colour chips labelled with these hex values: Ink #11150F, Olive enamel #52583B, Worn steel #767B68, Bakelite #392A1D, Tape #D6C7A5, Phosphor #D6B65E, Alarm #B73C28, Cyan optics #8ACDD5. Use olive/brown materials rather than washing the whole board green. Beneath chips place four macro material specimens labelled "ENAMEL", "BAKELITE", "GLASS", "TAPE". Make them convincing physical material samples with restrained wear and readable contrast. Warm amber phosphor is a small separate live-instrument lettering specimen only; never a glow on the off camera.

Lower left: two equal-size supervisor token concepts, clearly LIMEN and STILETTO, each chest-up within a rectangular rounded instrument intercom socket with an angled retaining latch, a tiny speaker grille and a small blank cream speech bubble visibly attached to that individual token. Readable full-colour portraits retain original cyan and red-orange optics, crisp facial/helmet identity and dark metal response; no monochrome green filter. Each speech bubble has a calm blank usable text area. Labels below tokens exactly "LIMEN" and "STILETTO". No dialogue baked into the bubbles.

Right middle: one purposeful sample COMMIT control, a broad olive physical hinged/tactile lever or heavy bakelite plunger with protected amber label, clearly labelled "COMMIT", not a red emergency-stop button. Beside it, four coherent small raised relief resource emblems on matching olive/bakelite tiles: stacked discs for "FUNDS", recognizably ROBOT worker head for "WORKERS", cog over short conveyor for "LINE", shipping crate for "DELIVERY". Consistent low-relief metal, front-on view, same light, same scale. Small red alarm lens specimen near the palette only, no flashing or fake live data.

Lower right: a compact neat set of six torn adhesive room-name tape specimens, in two short columns where needed, each handwritten clearly: "LATTICE FORGE", "SECURITY", "BURN-IN THEATRE", "COGNITIVE SUBSTRATE BREWERY", "WEAVING GALLERY", "CORTEX ASSEMBLY". Long brewery name can occupy two handwritten lines. These are label samples, not additional powered screens. Keep all six full names readable; do not abbreviate. Include a small clean amber phosphor sample reading "DAY 01" as a separate typography material specimen if space permits, unmistakably separate from the off monitor.

Lighting: one consistent top-left soft key light, warm neutral fill, subtle contact shadows, cinematic industrial material realism. Clear hierarchy and working surfaces, believable limited grime around joins and hand-contact edges; much quieter wear on text areas. No tutorial paragraphs, no fake readings on the off camera, no room art anywhere inside the big black glass, no greenwash, no cute mascot, no generic webpage cards. Do not merely recolour the baseline; redesign its hardware silhouette, grip, selector, portrait sockets and commit mechanism into serviceable retro field instrumentation.

referenced_images.role: Loopforge material/world reference; not inserted into the off camera
Baseline content/readability reference; hardware geometry reimagined

authorship: Generated original board based on the provided Loopforge references. Broad Pip-Boy / field instrumentation inspiration; no external franchise image provided or incorporated.
palette_note: These are authored implementation proposals, not sampled pixel values. Rendered hex captions are illustrative and may differ; use this JSON for exact colour values.

typography_proposal.headings_labels: IBM Plex Sans Condensed Medium/Semibold for compact physical labels; reserve widely spaced capitals for short headings.
typography_proposal.dynamic_data: IBM Plex Mono Regular/Medium for live native numbers and status text. Normal readable rendering; no mandatory simulated phosphor raster.
typography_proposal.speech: IBM Plex Sans Regular/Medium in the calm light bubble areas, as live semantic text.
typography_proposal.room_tapes: Custom hurried dark-pen lettering with accessible text equivalents; all full names remain readable.
typography_proposal.source_note: IBM's own font repository confirms Sans, Mono and Sans Condensed families and OFL availability; checked 2026-10-08. Font selection is an art-direction proposal, not identification of the generated letterforms.

rationale: Rounded serviceable cast housings, deep brown bakelite hand grips, captive slotted screws, a large tactile selector and hinged mechanical commit action change the baseline's construction and silhouette. Olive paint makes the console feel like maintained field equipment. Warm amber phosphor remains localized; cyan LIMEN optics and red STILETTO visor preserve Loopforge identities. Portraits use rectangular intercom sockets with latches instead of baseline round medallions.

inspection.limen_identity: Cracked mechanical skull, teeth/jaw assembly, cyan optics retained.
inspection.stiletto_identity: Closed dark angular helmet, red-orange T visor and mechanical neck retained.
inspection.bubbles: Two attached blank quiet speech areas; equal supervisor prominence.
inspection.resources: Funds / robot workers / line / delivery share matching low-relief finish and scale.
inspection.lighting: Consistent top-left soft light across hardware, tokens and samples.

tradeoffs_and_concerns: Physical depth and larger grips consume more width than the baseline; a six-camera composition must simplify repeated peripheral hardware to preserve phone readability.
The board is a source reference only, not a runtime asset; separate frame/glass/control assets and native text remain necessary.
Tiny generated palette captions are not authoritative colour specifications.

The generated monitor includes unlit engraved hardware selector legends such as REC/PLAY/DIAG. They are physical detents, not live camera readings; omit unsupported detent labels from production assets so off cameras convey only room identity.
Generated incidental branding/taglines are board decoration, not recommended product copy.
No full six-camera composition or mobile implementation was attempted within this one-board assignment.
